messages.subject: Barrier models
parts:
Hi,

I would like to try some barrier models on some dataset I have. Where could I find some R code with some examples? The section in the R website seems to be under construction at the moment.

Also, how scalable are these models? I am planning to use them on some noise data from my hometown where we have ~4000 buildings according to Open Street Map...

Many thanks.

Virgilio

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Barrier models
parts:
Hi Virgilio,

Yes, the website is actually under replacement :)

See https://haakonbakka.bitbucket.io/btopic107.html
- here you find a code example (comparing the different models) and links to explanations for the mesh
- the dataset/analysis is further explained in https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.03787

Let me know if you have any questions or feedback to the new site.

# Scalability

This should work on the same kind of problems as the stationary model. It will be slower, perhaps something like 3x.

Kind regards,
Haakon

Hi, 

I have a question regarding the output when a 'barrier.model' is used in the spde argument. Given that the output for the hyperparameters is in theta1 and theta2, what would be the correct way to calculate the nominal range and intercept? 

I guess it is not possible to use the inla.spde2.result function given that when I use it like this:
field <- inla.spde2.result(res, name='xi', barrier.model)
I get an error message 
Error in inla.require.inherits(spde, "inla.spde2", "'spde'") : 
  'spde' must inherit from class "inla.spde2".

(which of course makes sense unless I am not using the function properly for this kind of models)

Thank you
Nikos

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Barrier models
parts:
Haakon's barrier model code constructs rgeneric models. inla.spde.result() only handles inla.spde model objects and doesn’t know how to extract the needed information from those rgeneric models. Look at the code defining the barrier rgeneric model to see the details of the definition.  It’s on the todo-list to get this integrated into the package, to help with this...

Finn

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Barrier models
parts:
The two parameters of the barrier model is
theta1 = log(sigma)
theta2 = log(range)

So to look at the posterior marginals for the range, use
>> ?inla.tmarginal
with the exponential function.

I will be sure to add this to the documentation. Thank you for the question!

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Barrier models
parts:
Hi again,

I investigated some more, and there is one potential bug you may have found! We are fixing it right now. As a temporary measure (before you upgrade to the new INLA version today), you may use
>> + f(xi.AR1, model=barrier.model, n=mesh$n, group=xi.AR1.group, control.group = list(model = 'ar1'))
where I have added the input n=mesh$n (the same mesh as used to construct the barrier model.

Please avoid using this in the future (tomorrow) though! Update INLA instead :)

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
